items.stem: Define the term “a reducing sugar”.
items.answer: A sugar that reduces Fehling's solution and Tollens' reagent because it has a free aldehyde or ketone group.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a sugar that reduces Fehling's solution and Tollens' reagent because it has a free aldehyde or ketone group.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about carbohydrates is correct?
items.answer: Cellulose is a straight-chain polymer of β-D-glucose.
items.markingKey: (d) Cellulose is a straight-chain polymer of β-D-glucose. The other statements are false. In sucrose the reducing groups of both glucose and fructose are used in the glycosidic bond, so it is non-reducing. Cellulose is made of β-D-glucose units linked C1–C4. Maltose consists of two α-D-glucose units linked C1–C4.
options: Cellulose is a polymer of α-D-glucose.
Maltose consists of glucose and fructose.
Cellulose is a straight-chain polymer of β-D-glucose.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a polysaccharide?
items.answer: maltose
items.markingKey: (c) Maltose is a disaccharide, not a polysaccharide.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Sucrose is a reducing sugar.”
items.answer: In sucrose the reducing groups of both glucose and fructose are used in the glycosidic bond, so it is non-reducing.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: In sucrose the reducing groups of both glucose and fructose are used in the glycosidic bond, so it is non-reducing.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about carbohydrates is incorrect?
items.answer: Maltose consists of glucose and fructose.
items.markingKey: (c) The incorrect statement is “Maltose consists of glucose and fructose.” Correct form: Maltose consists of two α-D-glucose units linked C1–C4.
options: Glucose does not give Schiff's test, which supports its cyclic structure.
Cellulose is a straight-chain polymer of β-D-glucose.
Maltose consists of glucose and fructose.
Amylose is water soluble and forms 15–20% of starch.

items.stem:
A carbohydrate has these features: polymer of α-glucose; gives blue colour with iodine; amylose (15–20%) and amylopectin (80–85%).
(i) Identify the carbohydrate. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were sucrose? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Starch (ii) storage carbohydrate of plants (iii) gives invert sugar on hydrolysis; disaccharide of α-D-glucose and β-D-fructose
items.markingKey: (i) starch – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: storage carbohydrate of plants – 1 mark. (iii) for sucrose: disaccharide of α-D-glucose and β-D-fructose; C1–C2 glycosidic linkage; non-reducing sugar – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which of the following is a reducing sugar?
items.answer: fructose
items.markingKey: (c) Fructose is a reducing sugar; the others are not.

items.stem: A carbohydrate has these features: straight chain of β-D-glucose; cannot be digested by humans; C1–C4 β-glycosidic links. Identify the carbohydrate. Give a reason.
items.answer: Cellulose
items.markingKey: 1 mark: cellulose; 1 mark: the features straight chain of β-D-glucose; cannot be digested by humans; C1–C4 β-glycosidic links are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Ishita hydrolyses 342 g of sucrose with dilute acid: C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ + H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ (glucose) + C₆H₁₂O₆ (fructose). Calculate the mass of glucose formed. Why is this product mixture called invert sugar? (Molar masses: sucrose 342, glucose 180 g mol⁻¹)
items.answer: 180 g of glucose; the sign of rotation is inverted from dextro (sucrose) to laevo (mixture)
items.markingKey: n = 342/342 = 1.00 mol (1); glucose = 1.00 × 180 = 180 g (1); the rotation changes from dextro (sucrose) to laevo (mixture), because fructose (−92.4°) outweighs glucose (+52.5°) (1).

items.stem: Which term describes the storage polysaccharide of animals, structurally similar to amylopectin but more highly branched?
items.answer: glycogen
items.markingKey: (b) Glycogen: the storage polysaccharide of animals, structurally similar to amylopectin but more highly branched.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as reducing sugar or non-reducing carbohydrate: cellulose, glucose, maltose, lactose.
items.answer: cellulose – non-reducing carbohydrate; glucose – reducing sugar; maltose – reducing sugar; lactose – reducing sugar.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: cellulose – non-reducing carbohydrate; glucose – reducing sugar; maltose – reducing sugar; lactose – reducing sugar.

items.stem: Give two differences between lactose and maltose.
items.answer: Lactose: milk sugar; β-D-galactose and β-D-glucose. Maltose: C1–C4 glycosidic linkage; formed by the action of diastase on starch.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. lactose – milk sugar; β-D-galactose and β-D-glucose; maltose – C1–C4 glycosidic linkage; formed by the action of diastase on starch.

items.stem: A carbohydrate has these features: storage carbohydrate of plants; amylose (15–20%) and amylopectin (80–85%). Identify the carbohydrate.
items.answer: starch
items.markingKey: (c) Starch: storage carbohydrate of plants; amylose (15–20%) and amylopectin (80–85%).

items.stem: Classify each of the following as disaccharide or polysaccharide: maltose, cellulose, glycogen, starch.
items.answer: maltose – disaccharide; cellulose – polysaccharide; glycogen – polysaccharide; starch – polysaccharide.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: maltose – disaccharide; cellulose – polysaccharide; glycogen – polysaccharide; starch – polysaccharide.

items.stem: What is meant by “invert sugar”?
items.answer: The equimolar mixture of glucose and fructose formed by hydrolysis of sucrose, which is laevorotatory.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the equimolar mixture of glucose and fructose formed by hydrolysis of sucrose, which is laevorotatory.

items.stem: Which of the following is a disaccharide?
items.answer: maltose
items.markingKey: (c) Maltose is a disaccharide; the others are not.

items.stem: What is meant by “a peptide bond”?
items.answer: The amide linkage –CO–NH– formed between the –COOH group of one amino acid and the –NH₂ group of another.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the amide linkage –CO–NH– formed between the –COOH group of one amino acid and the –NH₂ group of another.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as essential amino acid or non-essential amino acid: glycine, leucine, phenylalanine, serine.
items.answer: glycine – non-essential amino acid; leucine – essential amino acid; phenylalanine – essential amino acid; serine – non-essential amino acid.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: glycine – non-essential amino acid; leucine – essential amino acid; phenylalanine – essential amino acid; serine – non-essential amino acid.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a non-essential amino acid?
items.answer: leucine
items.markingKey: (a) Leucine is an essential amino acid, not a non-essential amino acid.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Denaturation breaks the peptide bonds of a protein.”
items.answer: Denaturation destroys secondary and tertiary structures; the primary structure (peptide bonds) is intact.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Denaturation destroys secondary and tertiary structures; the primary structure (peptide bonds) is intact.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about proteins is incorrect?
items.answer: Denaturation breaks the peptide bonds of a protein.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “Denaturation breaks the peptide bonds of a protein.” Correct form: Denaturation destroys secondary and tertiary structures; the primary structure (peptide bonds) is intact.
options: Denaturation breaks the peptide bonds of a protein.
Boiling an egg denatures its proteins.
Glycine is the only common α-amino acid that is not optically active.
Amino acids exist as zwitterions in aqueous solution.

items.stem:
Nikita learns that she cannot make some amino acids in her body and must get them from dal, milk and eggs.
(i) What are such amino acids called? Give two examples. (2 marks)
(ii) Why do amino acids behave like salts? (1 mark)
(iii) Write the structure of the dipeptide Gly–Ala. (1 mark)
items.answer: (i) Essential amino acids, e.g. valine, leucine (lysine, phenylalanine). (ii) They exist as zwitterions (H₃N⁺–CHR–COO⁻). (iii) H₂N–CH₂–CO–NH–CH(CH₃)–COOH.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct order of levels of protein structure: primary, secondary, quaternary, tertiary. Give a reason.
items.answer: primary → secondary → tertiary → quaternary
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order primary → secondary → tertiary → quaternary; 1 mark for the reason: Sequence → local folding (α-helix/β-sheet) → overall folding → association of subunits.

items.stem: Calculate the number of peptide bonds and the molar mass of the peptide Val–Cys–Leu–Ser–Asp. (Molar masses in g mol⁻¹: valine 117, cysteine 121, leucine 131, serine 105, aspartic acid 133; water 18)
items.answer: 4 peptide bonds; 535 g mol⁻¹
items.markingKey: 5 amino acids join by 4 peptide bonds, losing 4 H₂O (1); M = 607 − 4 × 18 = 535 g mol⁻¹ (1).

items.stem: Which of the following is a fibrous protein?
items.answer: myosin
items.markingKey: (a) Myosin is a fibrous protein; the others are not.

items.stem: A level of protein structure has these features: lost on denaturation; held by H-bonds, disulphide links, van der Waals and electrostatic forces; overall folding of the chain. Which level of structure is described? Give a reason.
items.answer: Tertiary structure
items.markingKey: 1 mark: tertiary structure; 1 mark: the features lost on denaturation; held by H-bonds, disulphide links, van der Waals and electrostatic forces; overall folding of the chain are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between secondary structure and quaternary structure on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A level of protein structure has these features: hydrogen bonds between –CO and –NH groups. Which level of structure is described – secondary structure or quaternary structure? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Secondary structure: α-helix or β-pleated sheet; hydrogen bonds between –CO and –NH groups; local shape of the backbone. Quaternary structure: arrangement of two or more polypeptide subunits; shown by haemoglobin with four subunits; held by non-covalent forces. (b) Secondary structure.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: secondary structure; 1 mark: “hydrogen bonds between –CO and –NH groups” is a feature of secondary structure.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about proteins is correct?
items.answer: The primary structure of a protein is not changed on denaturation.
items.markingKey: (b) The primary structure of a protein is not changed on denaturation. The other statements are false. Denaturation destroys secondary and tertiary structures; the primary structure (peptide bonds) is intact. Glycine (H₂NCH₂COOH) has two H on the α-carbon and is optically inactive. It is held mainly by intramolecular hydrogen bonds between –NH and –C=O groups.
options: The primary structure of a protein is not changed on denaturation.
Denaturation breaks the peptide bonds of a protein.
The α-helix is held by disulphide bonds only.

items.stem: What happens to the structure of a protein when it is denatured? Give two examples of denaturation from daily life.
items.answer: Hydrogen bonds and other weak interactions are broken; the globules unfold and helices uncoil, so secondary and tertiary structures are lost and biological activity is lost, though the primary structure remains. Examples: coagulation of egg white on boiling; curdling of milk by lactic acid.
items.markingKey: 1 mark change; 1 mark two examples.

items.stem: Define the term “a zwitterion”.
items.answer: The dipolar ion formed when the –COOH group of an amino acid loses a proton to its own –NH₂ group.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the dipolar ion formed when the –COOH group of an amino acid loses a proton to its own –NH₂ group.

items.stem: How many different peptides containing each of glutamic acid, leucine and lysine exactly once are possible?
items.markingKey: (a) Order matters (N- and C-terminals are different) ⇒ 3! = 6 peptides.

items.stem: A level of protein structure has these features: not affected by denaturation; held by peptide bonds; any change gives a different protein. Which level of structure is described? Give a reason.
items.answer: Primary structure
items.markingKey: 1 mark: primary structure; 1 mark: the features not affected by denaturation; held by peptide bonds; any change gives a different protein are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Explain the term “a vitamin”.
items.answer: An organic compound required in small amounts in the diet for normal growth and health.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: an organic compound required in small amounts in the diet for normal growth and health.

items.stem: Which disease is caused by deficiency of vitamin D?
items.answer: rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults
items.markingKey: (a) Vitamin D deficiency: rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.
options: rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults
cheilosis (fissuring at the corners of the mouth and lips), digestive disorders
increased fragility of RBCs and muscular weakness

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Enzymes raise the activation energy of reactions.”
items.answer: They lower the activation energy.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: They lower the activation energy.

items.stem: Why must vitamin C be supplied regularly in our diet while vitamin A need not be?
items.answer: Vitamin C is water soluble and is readily excreted in urine, so it cannot be stored. Vitamin A is fat soluble and is stored in liver and adipose tissue.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem:
A doctor in Lucknow sees three children: one with bleeding gums, one with bow legs, and one who cannot see well in dim light.
(i) Identify the vitamin deficient in each. (3 marks)
(ii) Which of these vitamins are fat soluble? (1 mark)
items.answer: (i) Bleeding gums: vitamin C (scurvy); bow legs: vitamin D (rickets); poor dim-light vision: vitamin A (night blindness). (ii) Vitamins A and D.

items.stem: Explain how enzymes act as catalysts. How are they different from ordinary chemical catalysts?
items.answer: Enzymes provide a different pathway with lower activation energy; the substrate binds to the active site to form an enzyme–substrate complex that breaks down to products. They are proteins, highly specific, work at mild temperature and pH, and are needed in very small amounts.
items.markingKey: 1 mark mechanism; 1 mark differences.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about enzymes, vitamins and hormones is incorrect?
items.answer: Insulin raises the blood glucose level.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “Insulin raises the blood glucose level.” Correct form: Insulin lowers blood glucose; glucagon raises it.
options: Insulin raises the blood glucose level.
Vitamin B₁₂ is stored in the liver although it is water soluble.
Insulin and glucagon together keep the blood glucose level in a narrow range.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a steroid hormone?
items.answer: invertase
items.markingKey: (c) Invertase is an enzyme, not a steroid hormone.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Enzymes speed up reactions.
Reason (R): Enzymes lower the activation energy.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Lower Ea means faster rate.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: What is meant by “a fat-soluble vitamin”?
items.answer: A vitamin such as A, D, E or K that is stored in the liver and adipose tissue.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a vitamin such as A, D, E or K that is stored in the liver and adipose tissue.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about enzymes, vitamins and hormones is correct?
items.answer: Enzymes are highly specific in their action.
items.markingKey: (d) Enzymes are highly specific in their action. The other statements are false. Vitamin C is water soluble and must be taken regularly. Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets/osteomalacia; scurvy is due to vitamin C deficiency. Insulin lowers blood glucose; glucagon raises it.
options: Vitamin C is a fat-soluble vitamin.
Deficiency of vitamin D causes scurvy.
Insulin raises the blood glucose level.
Enzymes are highly specific in their action.

items.stem: Which of the following is a steroid hormone?
items.answer: progesterone
items.markingKey: (c) Progesterone is a steroid hormone; the others are not.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Deficiency of vitamin D causes scurvy.
Reason (R): Enzymes lower the activation energy of reactions.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets/osteomalacia; scurvy is due to vitamin C deficiency. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Explain the term “a phosphodiester linkage”.
items.answer: The link between the 5′ and 3′ carbons of the sugars of adjacent nucleotides through a phosphate group.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the link between the 5′ and 3′ carbons of the sugars of adjacent nucleotides through a phosphate group.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about nucleic acids is correct?
items.answer: The sugar in DNA is 2-deoxyribose.
items.markingKey: (a) The sugar in DNA is 2-deoxyribose. The other statements are false. RNA contains uracil in place of thymine. RNA contains ribose; DNA contains 2-deoxyribose. DNA is a double helix; RNA is usually a single strand.
options: DNA and RNA both have a double helix structure.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine and guanine with cytosine.
Reason (R): The sugar in RNA is 2-deoxyribose.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: RNA contains ribose; DNA contains 2-deoxyribose.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A nucleic acid has these features: bases A, G, C and T; can replicate and carries hereditary information; double-stranded helix. Identify the nucleic acid. Give a reason.
items.answer: DNA
items.markingKey: 1 mark: DNA; 1 mark: the features bases A, G, C and T; can replicate and carries hereditary information; double-stranded helix are characteristic of it.

items.stem: One strand of a DNA segment has the base sequence 5′-ACTAGAACGATC-3′. What is the sequence of the complementary strand (written 3′ → 5′)?
items.answer: 3′-TGATCTTGCTAG-5′
items.markingKey: (a) A pairs with T and G pairs with C: 3′-TGATCTTGCTAG-5′.

items.stem:
Kabir reads that a DNA sample from a plant contains 30% adenine.
(i) What percentages of thymine, guanine and cytosine are present? (2 marks)
(ii) Which bases pair by three hydrogen bonds? (1 mark)
(iii) Name the sugar present. (1 mark)
items.answer: (i) T 30%, G 20%, C 20%. (ii) Guanine and cytosine. (iii) 2-Deoxyribose (β-D-2-deoxyribose).

items.stem: Which of the following is a purine base?
items.answer: guanine
items.markingKey: (b) Guanine is a purine base; the others are not.

items.stem: Which term describes the observation that in double-stranded DNA the amount of A equals T and the amount of G equals C?
items.answer: Chargaff's rule
items.markingKey: (d) Chargaff's rule: the observation that in double-stranded DNA the amount of A equals T and the amount of G equals C.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “RNA contains thymine.”
items.answer: RNA contains uracil in place of thymine.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: RNA contains uracil in place of thymine.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a pyrimidine base?
items.answer: guanine
items.markingKey: (b) Guanine is a purine base, not a pyrimidine base.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The sugar in RNA is 2-deoxyribose.”
items.answer: RNA contains ribose; DNA contains 2-deoxyribose.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: RNA contains ribose; DNA contains 2-deoxyribose.

items.stem: Describe the structure of DNA. Give three differences between DNA and RNA and state the biological functions of each.
items.answer: DNA: two antiparallel polynucleotide strands of 2-deoxyribose, phosphate and bases A, G, C, T, coiled in a double helix with A=T and G≡C base pairing by hydrogen bonds. Differences: sugar (deoxyribose vs ribose), bases (T vs U), double vs single strand. Functions: DNA stores and transmits heredity and replicates; RNA (m-, t-, r-RNA) carries out protein synthesis.
items.markingKey: 2 marks structure; 2 marks differences; 1 mark functions.

items.stem: Give two differences between DNA and RNA.
items.answer: DNA: double-stranded helix; sugar is 2-deoxyribose. RNA: bases A, G, C and U; directs protein synthesis.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. DNA – double-stranded helix; sugar is 2-deoxyribose; RNA – bases A, G, C and U; directs protein synthesis.

items.stem: A sample of double-stranded DNA contains 20% guanine. Calculate the percentages of the other three bases.
items.answer: cytosine 20%; adenine 30%; thymine 30%
items.markingKey: Base pairing (Chargaff's rule): guanine = cytosine = 20% (1); remaining 60% is shared equally: adenine = thymine = 30% (1).

items.stem: What is the difference between a nucleoside and a nucleotide? Draw a simple scheme of the structure of a dinucleotide.
items.answer: Nucleoside = base + sugar (base at C1′); nucleotide = nucleoside + phosphate at C5′. Dinucleotide: base–sugar–phosphate–sugar–base, the phosphate joining C5′ of one sugar to C3′ of the next (phosphodiester link).
items.markingKey: 1 mark difference; 1 mark scheme.

items.stem: Calculate the number of peptide bonds and the molar mass of the peptide Gly–Ser–Asp. (Molar masses in g mol⁻¹: glycine 75, serine 105, aspartic acid 133; water 18)
items.answer: 2 peptide bonds; 277 g mol⁻¹
items.markingKey: 3 amino acids join by 2 peptide bonds, losing 2 H₂O (1); M = 313 − 2 × 18 = 277 g mol⁻¹ (1).

items.stem: Classify each of the following as fat-soluble vitamin or water-soluble vitamin: vitamin B₆, vitamin B₁, vitamin K, vitamin E.
items.answer: vitamin B₆ – water-soluble vitamin; vitamin B₁ – water-soluble vitamin; vitamin K – fat-soluble vitamin; vitamin E – fat-soluble vitamin.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: vitamin B₆ – water-soluble vitamin; vitamin B₁ – water-soluble vitamin; vitamin K – fat-soluble vitamin; vitamin E – fat-soluble vitamin.

items.stem:
A nucleic acid has these features: directs protein synthesis; sugar is ribose; bases A, G, C and U.
(i) Identify the nucleic acid. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were DNA? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) RNA (ii) usually single-stranded (iii) sugar is 2-deoxyribose; double-stranded helix
items.markingKey: (i) RNA – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: usually single-stranded – 1 mark. (iii) for DNA: sugar is 2-deoxyribose; bases A, G, C and T; double-stranded helix – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Define the term “the double helix”.
items.answer: The structure of DNA in which two complementary polynucleotide strands are coiled around a common axis.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the structure of DNA in which two complementary polynucleotide strands are coiled around a common axis.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Amylopectin is an unbranched chain.”
items.answer: Amylopectin is branched, with C1–C6 links at branch points.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Amylopectin is branched, with C1–C6 links at branch points.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a fat-soluble vitamin?
items.answer: vitamin B₆
items.markingKey: (b) Vitamin B₆ is a water-soluble vitamin, not a fat-soluble vitamin.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between RNA and DNA on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A nucleic acid has these features: can replicate and carries hereditary information. Identify the nucleic acid – RNA or DNA? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) RNA: sugar is ribose; bases A, G, C and U; usually single-stranded. DNA: sugar is 2-deoxyribose; bases A, G, C and T; double-stranded helix. (b) DNA.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: DNA; 1 mark: “can replicate and carries hereditary information” is a feature of DNA.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The α-helix is held by disulphide bonds only.”
items.answer: It is held mainly by intramolecular hydrogen bonds between –NH and –C=O groups.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: It is held mainly by intramolecular hydrogen bonds between –NH and –C=O groups.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a reducing sugar?
items.answer: starch
items.markingKey: (a) Starch is a non-reducing carbohydrate, not a reducing sugar.

items.stem: Which term describes a vitamin such as those of the B group or C that must be supplied regularly in the diet?
items.answer: a water-soluble vitamin
items.markingKey: (a) A water-soluble vitamin: a vitamin such as those of the B group or C that must be supplied regularly in the diet.

items.stem: A carbohydrate has these features: disaccharide of α-D-glucose and β-D-fructose; gives invert sugar on hydrolysis. Identify the carbohydrate. Give a reason.
items.answer: Sucrose
items.markingKey: 1 mark: sucrose; 1 mark: the features disaccharide of α-D-glucose and β-D-fructose; gives invert sugar on hydrolysis are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a fibrous protein?
items.answer: albumin
items.markingKey: (c) Albumin is a globular protein, not a fibrous protein.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between tertiary structure and quaternary structure on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A level of protein structure has these features: gives fibrous or globular shapes. Which level of structure is described – tertiary structure or quaternary structure? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Tertiary structure: overall folding of the chain; gives fibrous or globular shapes; held by H-bonds, disulphide links, van der Waals and electrostatic forces. Quaternary structure: arrangement of two or more polypeptide subunits; shown by haemoglobin with four subunits; held by non-covalent forces. (b) Tertiary structure.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: tertiary structure; 1 mark: “gives fibrous or globular shapes” is a feature of tertiary structure.

items.stem: A nucleic acid has these features: bases A, G, C and T; double-stranded helix. Identify the nucleic acid. Give a reason.
items.answer: DNA
items.markingKey: 1 mark: DNA; 1 mark: the features bases A, G, C and T; double-stranded helix are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Amylopectin is an unbranched chain.
Reason (R): Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Amylopectin is branched, with C1–C6 links at branch points. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Insulin raises the blood glucose level.”
items.answer: Insulin lowers blood glucose; glucagon raises it.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Insulin lowers blood glucose; glucagon raises it.

items.stem: Which term describes the loss of biological activity of a protein when its secondary and tertiary structures are destroyed by heat or pH change?
items.answer: denaturation
items.markingKey: (c) Denaturation: the loss of biological activity of a protein when its secondary and tertiary structures are destroyed by heat or pH change.

items.stem:
A carbohydrate has these features: cannot be digested by humans; main component of plant cell walls; straight chain of β-D-glucose.
(i) Identify the carbohydrate. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were starch? Give two points. (2 marks)
